__name: Town estates (EstateEvent): plots, houses, palace, rooms
__help: Pictures: "Atlas/Sprite" of the game, see docs/GameAssets/index.html (Buildings tab): TownCommon/..., CommonMapGrid/..., VillageCommon/...

Prices of houses, land and rooms are in price taxes: HouseTax x area x AreaWeight (area 10: x5), x2 in a city, inflation applied, the same for every buyer. Palace and Wall are in plain base taxes of the town (5 x 2^area, x2 in a city), paid from its budget. Growth: the price x this every level. TownBuildingCost: the sub-buildings of the towns (portal, auction, factory...) cost x this.

Growth: a mortal house grows up to MortalMaxBonus levels above its district's (a big population, a prosperous plot); NPC cultivators buy a house in a town of the area where they are (a city from NpcCityGrade, else a small town) and upgrade it with their spirit stones (at most NpcSpend of them, NpcShare of the plots); a spouse and the unmarried children live in the family house, a married child moves out in the same town; with NpcHomeChance a month an NPC goes back to its home town.

Clans: a cultivator with a house in the town and the living family (spouse, children, grandchildren). Relation -100..100 of two clans: a base moved by their fights + MemberWeight x the mean intimacy of their members + MarriageBonus a marriage between them. Yearly, hostile clans (HostileAt) brawl with BrawlChance (BrawlDeath: the loser dies), bitter enemies (WarAt) go to war with WarChance (WarDeath: each loser dies; the house is lost; a clan without members is wiped out). The player is asked to step in when its family or an ally (AllyAt) fights.

Houses: 6 levels; Width x Height = plots the house takes on the town map (a bigger house buys the plots around it); Tax = monthly tax in base taxes (x the Price of the district); Grade = cultivation grade needed.

Map: made once per town (terrain x main roads x palace in the middle or off it: 48 kinds, details at random; different in every save). A town grown into a city keeps its map in the middle of a bigger one. A new size only applies to the maps made after it.
